observed: On a59c2b8, Archive remote Python terminated with status 137 at 04:04:27 UTC; CI/CD/Smoke/V4 succeeded. The original grouped check first reported the then-incomplete Smoke, while the decisive Archive failure persisted. User-supplied host logs now record a global OOM killing python3 PID 307958 at 04:04:26 UTC, 4.145 GiB anonymous RSS, and the affected SSH session closing at 04:04:27. Another Python process held 1.817 GiB; total host RAM was approximately 7.841 GiB, without swap.
root_cause: The host exhausted allocatable memory and the kernel OOM killer killed a large Python process in the failed SSH time window. The archive implementation retains all full snapshots before filtering one lifecycle; this is a confirmed unbounded payload-retention defect and matches the failed job's resource behavior. Concurrent memory consumption and missing audit process budget aggravate the failure. The full historical command lines of the two Python PIDs were not captured, so exact per-workflow attribution remains unconfirmed; AliYunDunUpdate merely triggered allocation and is not established as the memory-pressure cause. The former unknown OOM hypothesis is now supported by explicit global_oom and Out of memory: Killed process records. SSH trust and release integrity passed; this was not the configured 20-minute timeout.
